cells.tense: Right now, with the pen in your hand.
cells.verb: opening to feel before you know what you'll feel
cells.place: where you take in the whole of a situation at once
cells.ask: stay open one beat past the moment the picture feels finished, and let what you know keep deepening instead of closing.
cells.core:
You're taking the whole thing in with your heart already open. Nothing has told you yet what to feel, and you're not rushing to decide — the picture is arriving and you're letting it. That openness is what makes your seeing wide instead of narrow.

There's more here if you want it. The picture never has to be done. Where you'd normally say "I see it now" and stop, you can leave the door open a beat longer — and what you know about this keeps growing instead of setting.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole of it with your heart open, and you're not done looking.

cells.tense: Ahead of yourself, bracing for what hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: opening to everything that might come before any of it comes
cells.place: where you take in the whole of a situation at once
cells.ask: pick one thing you already see clearly, choose it on purpose, and carry it through to finished — and the picture settles enough to keep deepening on its own.
cells.core:
You're wide open to what's coming, and it hasn't come yet. Every version of how this might feel is already in you, so the whole picture never gets to settle — it keeps shifting with each new thing you're ready to receive. You're bracing to take in a future that hasn't been written.

The way back isn't closing. It's finishing. Somewhere in all that openness there's one thing you can already see plainly. Choose it, from what's clear and not from what you're afraid of, and take it to the end. One thing done lets the rest of the picture stop moving long enough to be known.
cells.sheetLine: You're open to a future you can't take in yet, and the picture won't hold still.

cells.tense: Behind you, at a door that already closed.
cells.verb: closing before anything has a chance to arrive
cells.place: where you take in the whole of a situation at once
cells.ask: take one thing that already came true for you and spend an hour inside it as if it were new — and the knowing starts moving again on its own.
cells.core:
You can still see the whole picture. You're just seeing it from behind glass. Somewhere back there, taking something in cost too much, and now the heart shuts before anything new gets through — so what you see arrives already decided, already filed, already a little bit over.

Don't try to pry yourself open; that's pushing on an empty room. Go instead to something that has actually become real in your life — something that once was only possible and now exists — and be in it like it's the first time. Fresh contact with what already came true is what refills the place that stopped receiving.
cells.sheetLine: You still see it all. You stopped letting it in.

cells.tense: Here, now, with the pen set down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: taking things in with your heart before your head has caught up
cells.place: where you take in the whole of a situation at once
cells.ask: name one thing you felt about this before you had a reason for it, and let "I don't know why yet" be enough — and the knowing keeps deepening because it's finally yours.
cells.core:
The whole picture is already landing in you — you felt the shape of this before you had a single reason for it — but you'd describe yourself as just being objective, just noticing. The openness is doing the work. You're crediting the analysis.

Try something smaller than analysis. There's a thing you knew about this situation directly, with no argument attached, and it has been proving right. Say that one, out loud, as a felt thing and not a conclusion. You don't have to explain it. Owning the knowing you already have is what lets it keep growing.
cells.sheetLine: You already felt the whole of it. You keep calling it observation.
